pages.source:
Exam Date & Time: 29-Jun-2022 (09:00 AM - 12:00 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  SECOND SEMESTER B.TECH. EXAMINATIONS (MIT BANGALORE) - JUNE/JULY 2022  
  SUBJECT : CSE_1051 - PROBLEM SOLVING USING COMPUTERS  
  PROBLEM SOLVING USING COMPUTERS [CSE-1051]  
Marks: 50                                                                               Duration: 180 mins.  
  A  
Answer all the questions.  
1A)          Write an algorithm and draw a flowchart to check if a given number is a spy number.  
  Hint: A number where the sum of all the digits is equal to the product of the digits is  
  known as a spy number.                                                                    (4)  
  e.g: Spy Numbers: 123, 1214  
  Not Spy Numbers: 1441, 45  
  
1B)           Write the basic structure of a C Program. Discuss each section briefly with suitable  
  example.                                                                                   (3)  
  
$$1C)           Evaluate the following expressions, given a=3, b=5, c=9, p=10, q=8, r=11, m=5, n=4,$$  
  x=12, y=2, z=6. Show all the intermediate steps.  
  i) x/y + z - m*y < y + p/m*a + r                                                           (3)  
  $$ii) n * q < = 3 * m + c / a$$  
  $$iii) (m /n != q - 5) && (b>a)$$  
  
2A)           Write a C program using nested if else statements to check whether a student is eligible  
  for scholarship or not. The user needs to enter the total of six subject marks (each out of  
  100) and the program checks the student's eligibility for scholarship. The student is  
  given full scholarship if the total marks is greater than or equal to 540, 50% scholarship (3)  
  if total marks is greater than or equal to 480, 20% if the total marks is greater than or  
  equal to 400. Any other marks other than mentioned are not eligible for scholarship.  
  
2B)           Write a C program using do-while loop to print the multiplication table upto 12 terms     (3)  
  for a given number. The table should be printed for all numbers entered by the user until

-1 as given in sample input/output:  
  
  
2C)   Given a 1D array of integers, perform the following tasks:  
  Task-1: Identify 2 integers in the given 1D array for which the product is the maximum  
  amongst all the products. Display the indices for these 2 integers.  
  Task-2: Identify 2 integers in the given 1D array for which the product is the minimum  
  amongst all the products. Display the indices for these 2 integers.  
  
  (4)  
  
  
3A)   Write a C program to read a 2D array and print it in the matrix form, with sum of all  
  elements in each row, at the end of each row.                                            (3)  
  
3B)   Write a C program to check whether the entered number is an Armstrong Number using  
  User-defined Function.  
  Hint: An Armstrong number is an integer such that the sum of the cubes of its digits is (3)  
  equal to the number itself.  
  
3C)   Write a C function TwoPrime () to check whether a given number can be expressed as  
  sum of two prime numbers, if so, display the 2 prime numbers, otherwise specify that  
  the number cannot be expressed as sum of two prime numbers. Write a main() function  
  which reads n numbers and prints the result by calling above function for each number.  
  Sample Input/Output:  
  $$Enter n = 3, Enter Numbers: 11 , 12 , 14                                                 (4)$$  
  Output:  
  11 cannot be expressed as sum of 2 prime numbers:  
  $$12 = 5 + 7$$  
  $$14 = 7 + 7$$

4A)             Write any 4 differences between recursion and iteration.  
  (2)  
  
4B)             Write a C program to check if the given number is a prime or not using recursion.  
  (3)  
  
4C)             Define a structure student to store the name and marks for 3 courses of a student. Write  
  a C program to read the data of N students using the structure defined and display the  
  same. Compute the average marks and display the name with the computed average for (5)  
  each student. Using the computed average score, display the name of the topper (student  
  with a maximum average score) without sorting.  
  
5A)             Define a structure Customer with customer_id, customer_name, Acc_open_date (date  
  can be an array of 3 integers) and acct_balance as its members. Using this structure,  
  write a C program to read the information of three (3) customers and print the details of (3)  
  customer having highest account balance.  
  
5B)             Define a structure employee with Name, no_of_days and salary as its members. Write  
  a C program using above structure, to calculate three employees (use array of sructures)  
  salary based on number of days worked. Use pointer to access the members of the          (3)  
  structure. Assume a remuneration of Rs. 750 per day to calculate the salary.  
  
5C)             Discuss on different areas where computers are used to commit crimes with suitable  
  examples.                                                                                 (4)  
  
  
-----End-----
